page: Microsoft Azure E2as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz, providing two virtual CPUs backed by one physical core with two threads. The architecture features an x86_64 instruction set with modern extensions including AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16), SHA-NI, and VAES. Cache provisioning consists of 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a dedicated 32 MB allocation of L3 cache.

Resource allocation follows a memory-optimized ratio of 8 GB per core, yielding 16.0 GB of system memory for the two vCPUs. The E2as_v7 does not include integrated GPUs or local instance storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent storage. Benchmark testing shows that memory subsystem throughput reaches 43.28 GB/s for large uncached reads and 33.7 GB/s for large block writes, aligning with mid-tier memory bandwidth tiers.

Benchmark results highlight an asymmetry between single-threaded execution and multi-core throughput. Single-core stress-ng tests place the instance in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, alongside high single-threaded data compression rates of 40.52 GB/s in gzip and 18.03 GB/s in bzip3 decompression. However, because overall compute capability is bounded by two vCPUs on a single physical core, multi-core stress-ng metrics, aggregate PassMark CPU scores (5089.01), and multi-threaded throughput tests settle into the bottom 25 percent.

Given its high per-core RAM capacity and fast single-thread execution, the instance offers a viable profile for light database instances, caching layers, and applications limited by memory capacity rather than parallel computation. It is less suitable for high-concurrency transactional processing or compute-heavy parallel workloads that require larger core counts.
description: Microsoft Azure E2as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. Configured with 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with two threads, the instance features 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX-512 instructions (including VNNI and BF16) and a 32 MB L3 cache. It lacks local ephemeral storage and dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier single-core performance, demonstrated by high stress-ng metrics and compression rates, but aggregate multi-threaded capacity remains constrained by the 2-vCPU hardware footprint. With average large-block memory bandwidth of 43.28 GB/s read and 33.7 GB/s write, the instance is technically aligned with memory-sensitive, single-thread-dependent workloads such as small memory-bound databases, in-memory caches, and light backend services.
